(i) Prove that the Jordan block Jn(λ) =        λ 1 0 · · · 0 0 λ 1 · · · 0 ... ... . . . . . . ... 0 0 · · · λ 1 0 0 · · · 0 λ        is similar to its transpose Jn(λ)t. Hint: Let e1, . . . , en be the standard basis of F n. Let P = (en, en−1, . . . , e1). Show that P −1Jn(λ)P = Jn(λ)t. (ii) Prove that every A ∈ Mn×n(C) is similar to its transpose At. (iii) Let Jn(λ) ∈ Mn×n(C) be a Jordan block with |λ| < 1. Prove that lim N →∞ Jn(λ) N = 0. (iv) Let A ∈ Mn×n(C) be such that all eigenvalues satisfy |λ| < 1. Prove that lim N →∞ AN = 0. Problem 3. Let A, N ∈ Mn×n(F ) with N = Jn(0) and AN = N A. Let e1, . . . , en be the standard basis of F n. We have seen in Example 11.12 that N ke1 = e1+k for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 1. (i) Suppose Ae1 = a11e1 + a21e2 + · · · + an1en. Let p(x) = a11 + a21x + · · · + an1xn−1 ∈ F [x]. Show that Ae1 = p(N )e1. (ii) Show that Aek = p(N )ek for 1 ≤ k ≤ n. (iii) Conclude that A = p(N ). Problem 4. (i) Find an example of matrices in Mn×n(C) such that Ak → A where Ak are diagonalizable but A is not diagonalizable. (ii) Find an example of matrices in Mn×n(C) such that Ak → A where Ak are not diagonalizable and A is diagonalizable. (iii) Show that for any A ∈ Mn×n(C) there exists a sequence of diagonalizable ma- trices Ak ∈ Mn×n(C) such that Ak → A. In other words, diagonalizable matrices are dense in Mn×n(C). Hint: Try manipulating the Jordan canonical form directly. Corollary 10.12 is very useful here. 1 Optional exercises related to Lecture 12 Do NOT submit this with your homework.
